obligations.note: Head payments.py required_approvals returns 2 only when amount > DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD, so a payment of exactly 10000.00 needs one approver. PAY-1 requires two distinct approvers at or above 10000.00, and is_fully_approved uses the same function. No exception covers PAY-1.
Ticket CHG-24576 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components payments.payments and payments.tests cover payments.py and tests/test_approvals_remaining.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author Sofia Santos, gave a code_review approval. Her directory emails do not overlap the author's.
The code_review approval names head commit 411570a56bdcf6c17bc3b2a1d313f38e789aee32, and there is no later commit.

records/ci/run.json records success on 4655e99d, not on head 411570a56. The later commit, "Simplify threshold check," changes >= to > in required_approvals, so the earlier full-suite pass does not cover the merged code, including the PAY-1 control test.
The change touches payments.payments and payments.tests, both marked security_sensitive false, so a security_review approval is not required.
Neither changed path is under controls/protected-paths.json, so a control_owner approval is not required.
The ticket type is standard and change.emergency is false, so a post-implementation review is not due.

The dual-control boundary is a deviation from PAY-1, and the register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to PAY-1 and payments.payments. The other exceptions are withdrawn, expired, or for other obligations.

Acceptance record ACR-0401 covers required_approvals with an exhaustive proof that two approvals are required iff amount >= 10000.00, on commit d30b2ad. This change alters that comparison, and the packet has no replacement exhaustive evidence on head.

summary: The change adds a payments-queue helper and, in the same file, changes dual control so a payment of exactly 10000.00 needs one approval instead of two. That violates PAY-1, and no valid exception excuses it. Prior exhaustive proof of the old >= rule lapses because required_approvals changed behavior, and CI passed only on the earlier commit, not on head. Independent approval, the ticket, and the non-emergency, non-sensitive scope are in order, but the dual-control break requires rejection.
